change.title: Keep restored history stopped until an explicit one-click
change.summary: Removes the frontend's automatic one_click_login call after a successful history restore so one user action submits only the restore_history_choice IPC, preserves the backend stopped result, and tells the user to start explicitly in a separate action.

basis: successful restoreHistoryChoice submits only restore_history_choice and never chains one_click_login, finalize_consumer_state, or status
the successful frontend message preserves the backend restore result and explicitly states that Science remains stopped until the user clicks one-click again
restore failure remains a single rejected restore IPC and cannot start the runtime
the backend restore operation, exact managed Science stop, credential publication, reference rotation, and narrow success DTO remain unchanged
manual one-click remains a separate explicit frontend action with the existing finalize-consumer readback contract
focused frontend tests, quality metadata validation, documentation governance, exact-SHA source gate, and clean-context review are required for source closure
a combined durable restore-and-resume transaction, O1-A, C1, F1-A, artifact, installed, live provider or Science, signing, and release behavior remain excluded
